data.turoyo: Məd nafəq u gelano qamayto, raġyo kowe, <...> u yawmo bu yawmo kəzzən kmanṭən ter daq qanyonaṯṯe, d maʕləfənne.
data.translation: Wenn das Gras hervorkommt, ist es zunächst zart, <...> (Die Bauern) gehen und bringen täglich (Gras) in ausreichender Menge, um ihre Kühe zu füttern.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell (1 existing) and evidence for the gloss clarification: retain the grass antecedent and mark the intervening cut explicitly.

before: füttern; to feed cattle with food made from ḥeṭe, sʕore, etc. you cannot ʕlf a cat or a dog! (p.c. Ilyas 18/08/25)
after: füttern; to feed cattle with food made from ḥeṭe, sʕore, etc. you cannot ʕlf a cat or a dog! (p.c. Ilyas 18/08/25); im Korpus auch mit frischem Gras als Futter (JTM 1.1/65).
rationale: The fresh-grass discourse explicitly supplies the feed for cattle; add this documented food type while retaining the native-speaker restriction and attribution verbatim. The animal restriction is not broadened.

summary: The JTM passage explicitly introduces u gelo and the daily collection of enough fodder for cattle before maʕləfənne. This supports grass as a feed type, not a general “feed any animal” meaning.

The attributed Ilyas statement, including its date and its cat/dog restriction, is preserved verbatim in the revised gloss. The corpus observation is appended so that the discrepancy remains visible to the editors.
The new plural object suffix -ne and the inherited full horse NP realize the same transitive feeding construction. No Detransitive or light-verb construction is demonstrated.
The inherited Infectum-wa example is retained. Neither supplied occurrence provides a new form box.

How should the native-speaker grain-based restriction be reconciled with fresh-grass feeding in JTM 1.1/65: dialect, type of prepared fodder, or a broader use? The current gloss retains both pieces of evidence.
Fresh grass is used to feed cattle in addition to the grain-based feed mentioned in the attributed note; the animal class remains livestock.
